a.raw: its spring in narnia and the witchs winter is over
a.fixed: It’s spring in Narnia, and the Witch’s winter is over.
a.why: It’s means it is. Narnia is a place name. Witch’s shows the winter was hers. A comma goes before and.

b.raw: mr beaver couldnt say a word when he heard about his dam
b.fixed: Mr. Beaver couldn’t say a word when he heard about his dam.
b.why: Mr. Beaver is a title and a name. Couldn’t joins could and not.

glossary.m: a thing in a story that stands for a bigger idea, like snow standing for the Witch's cold power
two words joined into one, with an apostrophe where letters were left out, like didn't
a word that shows who something belongs to, like Lucy's bottle
the little mark ’ that joins two words or shows belonging
a word that can stand on its own before an ending is added. Hope is the base word in hoping.
a funny poem with five lines and a bouncy beat
telling the truth, even when it is hard

cards.title: World Notes: Real Wolves
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: Real gray wolves live in family groups called packs. They are shy and usually stay far away from people.
Old fairy tales often made wolves the villains, like the wolf in Little Red Riding Hood.
In the story, Maugrim is a made-up wolf who works for the Witch. Real wolves are not like him.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Look back at Chapters 10 to 12. Lewis keeps bringing back signs of hope. Pick the one that matters most to you.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: roll together words, fix a passage in passes, and roll words with endings.
transcripts.guide2: Look back at Chapters 10 to 12 for your best details.
transcripts.guide3: Today you polish your literary response.

notes.wordParts: The word parts com- and con- both mean with or together. combine = to join together. connect = to tie together.
notes.grammar: An apostrophe has two jobs. It joins two words: did + not = didn’t. It shows belonging: Lucy’s bottle is the bottle that belongs to Lucy.
notes.spelling: Some endings change the base word. Double the last letter: run → running. Drop the silent e: hope → hoping. Change y to i: carry → carried.
notes.wgrd: Lewis keeps bringing back signs of hope: Father Christmas, the thaw, the spring flowers. A symbol lets the reader feel the idea, not just hear it.
vocab: made new again; restored to a fresh state
a person or thing that announces something important is coming
cheerful and friendly; in high spirits

plate.alt: A painting of branches covered in white blossoms against a bright blue sky
plate.credit: Almond Blossom · Vincent van Gogh, 1890 · Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam · Public domain
plate.look: A painting by Vincent van Gogh from 1890. He made it for his brother, whose baby son had just been born. Almond trees are among the first to bloom in spring, so the blossoms stood for new life. A real symbol! In Chapters 11 and 12, spring flowers stand for the end of the Witch's winter.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: The dwarf tells the Witch the truth: this is no thaw, this is Spring, and it is Aslan's doing.
items.why: He tells her the truth, even though she will not like it.

items.t: The Witch tells the Fox he will be forgiven if he says he has been lying.
items.why: She wants him to call the truth a lie.

items.t: Aslan tells Peter he has forgotten to clean his sword, and Peter blushes because it is true.
items.why: Peter does not make excuses. He fixes it.
